question: Finding work
label: Payroll job change since 2019
small_n_note: Under 1,000 payroll jobs: a few jobs move the percentage a lot
source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
note: Average employment covered by unemployment insurance over the latest four quarters vs. the 2019 average. Payroll jobs only; excludes farm proprietors and the self-employed, which matters most in farm counties (see All jobs).

question: Finding work
label: All jobs including the self-employed, change since 2019
source: BEA county employment (CAEMP25N)
note: Full- and part-time jobs including farm and nonfarm proprietors, BEA, by place of work. BEA's county employment currently ends in 2022.

question: Finding work
label: Share of private jobs in a different sector than in 2019
legend: Below 3%|3% to 4%|4% to 5%|5% to 6%|6% to 7%|7% or more
source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
note: The share of a county's private payroll jobs that would have to move to another sector to restore its 2019 mix: half the sum of the changes in each sector's share of private jobs, over the 10 private NAICS supersectors BLS publishes for counties, latest four quarters against 2019. Government is left out because it is an ownership category, not an industry. A county is shown only when BLS publishes private jobs and every private sector in every month of both periods, so every value is measured the same way. Yearly shifts mostly persist rather than reverse, which real change and BLS recoding an employer both do, so the map shows how far the mix moved, not why. Jobs BLS assigns to no county grew in office sectors over the same years, so a county that lost those sectors may have lost them to that statewide line; Douglas County is the clearest case. The latest quarters are preliminary.

note: Farm and nonfarm proprietors / all full- and part-time jobs, BEA.

source: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture
note: Federal government program payments received / market value of products sold, Census of Agriculture. Includes conservation and commodity programs.

source: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture

unit: dollars paid per $100 of premium, all crops
source: USDA Risk Management Agency, Summary of Business
note: Indemnities / total premium over the latest three complete crop years, all insured crops including rangeland. Above 100 means claims paid exceeded premium. A sign of crop or pasture losses, mostly from weather.

source: USDA Risk Management Agency, Summary of Business
note: Net reported acres on corn crop insurance policies, latest complete crop year vs. 2019. Most corn acres are insured, so it moves with planted acres, but it is not a planting count.

source: Nebraska Department of Revenue net taxable sales, excluding motor vehicles
note: Calendar-year net taxable sales by sellers located in the county, excluding motor vehicles (taxed separately), in 2019 dollars. Excludes sellers outside Nebraska (mostly online), which are about 30% of the state total. Not adjusted for changes in what is taxable.

question: Schools
label: TEEOSA aid per formula student, students living in the county (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA state aid certified for each school system, divided by its formula students. A district that crosses county lines is split by where its 2020 Census children ages 5-17 lived, so county figures are estimates. Includes equalization, foundation, option enrollment, allocated income tax and community achievement plan aid. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Schools
label: State share of school General Fund receipts, students living in the county (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: State sources as a share of the four General Fund receipt totals districts report in NDE's Annual Financial Reports (local sources 01-1-01000-000, county and ESU 01-1-02000-000, state sources 01-1-03000-000 and federal sources 01-1-04000-000), as reported. Property tax credits the state pays are state sources; the LB 1107 income tax credit, which districts booked as local taxes, stays local. Districts that cross county lines are split by where their 2020 Census children ages 5-17 lived, so county figures are estimates. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Schools
label: State share of school General Fund receipts, change since 2019-20 (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: Change in state sources' share of school districts' General Fund receipts, 2019-20 to the latest Annual Financial Report, in percentage points. Most of the rise is property tax credits, which grow with school taxes, so it is largest where taxable valuation per student is highest. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Schools
label: State share of school General Fund receipts, credits counted as local (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: The same General Fund receipts as the state share, with property tax credits (03131) and homestead exemption reimbursement (03130) counted as local. Credits pay part of a property tax the school board levies, so this reading treats them as the state paying local taxpayers' bills rather than funding schools. Districts that cross county lines are split by where their 2020 Census children ages 5-17 lived, so county figures are estimates. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Schools
label: State share with credits counted as local, change since 2019-20 (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: Change in the state share with property tax credits and homestead reimbursement counted as local, 2019-20 to the latest Annual Financial Report, in percentage points. Set beside the change in the reported state share, it shows how much of the rise is credits. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Schools
label: Share of students in districts receiving equalization aid (estimate)
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: Equalization aid goes only to systems whose formula need exceeds their resources, mostly local property tax capacity. Districts crossing county lines are split by 2020 Census children ages 5-17, so county figures are estimates. Students are counted where they live, not where they attend; option enrollment moves some across district lines.

question: Property taxes
label: Real property taxes levied, change since 2019
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: All property taxes levied in the county by every taxing authority, before property tax credits, deflated by the Midwest CPI-U. Tax year 2025 is levied in fall 2025 and paid in 2026.

question: Property taxes
label: Real taxable valuation, change since 2019
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: Taxable valuation of all property in the county as Revenue reports it with taxes levied, deflated by the Midwest CPI-U. This is the value levies apply to, not the school adjusted valuation TEEOSA uses for local effort.

question: Property taxes
label: Agricultural land and buildings' share of taxable valuation
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: Taxable valuation of agricultural land plus agricultural buildings and farmsite land / all taxable valuation. Agricultural land is taxed at 75% of market value.

question: Property taxes
label: Real property taxes after state credits, change since 2019
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: Taxes levied minus the state credits applied to them, the Property Tax Credit Act credit, the LB 1107 income tax credit (school taxes for tax years 2019 to 2022, community college taxes from 2021; tax year 2023 counts individual returns only, and later years are not yet published) and the School District Property Tax Relief Credit (from 2024), deflated by the Midwest CPI-U. County amounts are Revenue's certifications from 2022 on; earlier real property credits and all LB 1107 credits are split to counties from statewide totals and are estimates. The color breaks are shifted down because nearly every county fell.

question: Property taxes
label: Share of property taxes paid by state credits
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: Property Tax Credit Act credit plus School District Property Tax Relief Credit / all property taxes levied in the county.

question: Property taxes
label: School districts' share of property taxes
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: School district general fund and bond taxes / all property taxes levied in the county.

question: Property taxes
label: Average property tax rate
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: All property taxes levied / all taxable valuation, per $100. Agricultural land is assessed at 75% of market value and other property at 100%, so in ag-heavy counties the tax per $100 of market value is lower than this rate.

question: Property taxes
label: Agricultural land and buildings' share of property taxes
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue, value and taxes levied by subdivision and property type, and property tax credit certifications
note: Taxes levied on agricultural land plus agricultural buildings and farmsite land / all property taxes levied. Farm homes count as residential, as Revenue reports them.

question: Aid

source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: All TEEOSA state aid certified for the system (equalization, foundation, option enrollment, allocated income tax and community achievement plan aid) divided by formula students.

question: Spending
label: State share of General Fund receipts, credits counted as local
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: The system's state share of General Fund receipts with property tax credits (03131) and homestead exemption reimbursement (03130) counted as local money. Credits pay part of the property tax the school board levies, so this reading treats them as the state paying local taxpayers' bills.

question: Spending
label: Spending per student, NDE per pupil cost
source: Nebraska Department of Education per pupil cost reports, with ADM from NDE's ADA and ADM lookup
note: NDE's published per pupil cost. Adjusted current expense from the Annual Financial Report (instruction, student and staff services, administration, operations, transportation and summer school, with federal programs, less tuition and transportation paid to other districts and capital outlay) plus 3% of the value of buildings and contents, divided by the same school year's average daily membership (ADM).

question: Spending
label: Real spending per student, change since 2019-20
source: Nebraska Department of Education per pupil cost reports, with ADM from NDE's ADA and ADM lookup
note: NDE's per pupil cost, deflated to 2019 dollars with the Midwest CPI averaged over each school year, September to August. It includes federal spending, which rose with pandemic relief from 2020-21 and fell back in 2024-25.

question: Spending
label: State share of General Fund receipts
source: Nebraska Department of Education school district Annual Financial Reports (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: State sources as a share of the four General Fund receipt totals districts report in NDE's Annual Financial Reports (local sources 01-1-01000-000, county and ESU 01-1-02000-000, state sources 01-1-03000-000 and federal sources 01-1-04000-000), as the system reported them.

question: Taxes
label: General Fund and Special Building levy (under the $1.05 limit)
source: Nebraska Department of Education LC-2 school district budget forms (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: The General Fund and Special Building property tax requests on the district's LC-2 budget form, divided by its certified taxable valuation, per $100. These are the two levies the $1.05 statutory limit covers; voters can approve an override above it. Bond levies for voter-approved bonds sit outside the limit and are not included. The top color marks districts at or within a cent of the limit; the one below it, districts from $0.95.

question: Taxes
label: General Fund property tax levy
source: Nebraska Department of Education LC-2 school district budget forms (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: The General Fund property tax request on the district's LC-2 budget form divided by its certified taxable valuation, per $100. Special Building and bond levies are not included. The $1.05 limit applies to the General Fund and Special Building levies together; see Levy under the limit.

question: Taxes
label: Unused property tax request authority
source: Nebraska Department of Education LC-2 school district budget forms (FOS Data Searches and Tables)
note: The part of the district's property tax request authority under LB 243 (2023) that it did not request, as a share of total authority (base authority plus any amount added by a 70% school board vote or by voters), from the LC-2 budget form. Under 1% means the district requested its full authority.

question: Aid
label: Receives equalization aid
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: Equalization aid is formula need minus resources, when need is larger. Resources are mostly local effort, $1.00 per $100 of the system's school adjusted valuation, plus other receipts and other state aid. Systems whose resources cover need receive none.

question: Aid
label: School adjusted valuation per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: The school adjusted valuation TEEOSA uses to compute local effort (local effort divided by the $1.00 rate), per formula student. It exists only inside the formula, as the yardstick for a system's theoretical local resources; it sets no one's taxes. Taxable valuation is under Ag share and Taxable valuation vs. 2019.

question: Taxes
label: Taxable valuation per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue certified School Adjusted Value
note: Taxable valuation per formula student, the October before the aid year. Taxable valuation is the value county assessors set, and the base levies and taxes apply to. A system with less of it needs a higher levy to raise the same dollars per student. It is not the school adjusted valuation the formula uses for local effort, which counts agricultural land at 72% of actual value against 96% for most other real property.

question: Aid
label: Formula need per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA formula need, built from basic funding plus allowances for poverty, English learners, transportation and other costs, per formula student. Small and sparse systems cost more per student.

question: Aid
label: Poverty allowance per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA poverty allowance, net of its correction, per formula student. Systems that do not claim the allowance show under the lowest bin. The district page breaks formula need into every component and compares any base year.

question: Aid
label: Limited English proficiency allowance per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA limited English proficiency allowance, net of its corrections, per formula student.

question: Aid
label: Special receipts allowance per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA special receipts allowance, which counts special education and certain other receipts in need, per formula student.

question: Aid
label: Transportation allowance per formula student
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA transportation allowance per formula student. Sparse systems with long routes need the most.

question: Taxes
label: Agricultural share of taxable valuation
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue certified School Adjusted Value
note: Agricultural land plus agricultural buildings and homesites, share of the system's taxable valuation (the unadjusted values in Revenue's School Adjusted Value report).

question: Students
label: Formula students, change since 2019-20
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: Formula students, the student count TEEOSA uses, 2019-20 aid year vs. the latest. Systems formed by reorganization since 2019-20 have no base year.

question: Taxes
label: Real taxable valuation, change since 2019
source: Nebraska Department of Revenue certified School Adjusted Value
note: The system's taxable valuation (Revenue's unadjusted value, all counties it covers), October 2019 to the latest October, deflated by the Midwest CPI-U. Systems formed since 2019 have no base.

question: Aid
label: Real TEEOSA aid per formula student, change since 2019-20
source: Nebraska Department of Education TEEOSA state aid certification
note: TEEOSA aid per formula student in 2019 dollars. Foundation aid, which began in 2023-24 and goes to every system regardless of its school adjusted valuation, explains most of the rise for systems without equalization aid. The upper breaks are wide for that reason.

question: Results
label: NSCAS English language arts, percent on track or advanced
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Students who scored on track or advanced on NSCAS English language arts, grades 3 to 8, as a percent of students tested, from NDE's own all-grades totals. NDE stopped publishing those totals with its 2025-26 release, so this shows the latest year it did, labeled by year, until 2025-26 totals appear. NDE withholds a total when the group is small or its percent is extreme, so some systems are blank. Scores track poverty closely, so read them beside the system's students.

question: Results
label: NSCAS mathematics, percent on track or advanced
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Students who scored on track or advanced on NSCAS mathematics, grades 3 to 8, as a percent of students tested, from NDE's own all-grades totals. NDE stopped publishing those totals with its 2025-26 release, so this shows the latest year it did, labeled by year, until 2025-26 totals appear. NDE withholds a total when the group is small or its percent is extreme, so some systems are blank. Scores track poverty closely, so read them beside the system's students.

question: Results
label: NSCAS science, percent on track or advanced
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Students who scored on track or advanced on NSCAS science (grades 5 and 8), as a percent of students tested, from NDE's own all-grades totals. NDE stopped publishing those totals with its 2025-26 release, so this shows the latest year it did, labeled by year, until 2025-26 totals appear. NDE withholds a total when the group is small or its percent is extreme, so about half of systems are blank.

question: Results
label: College-going rate
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: class of 2023, enrolled by October 2025 (Nebraska Education Profile)
note: The share of a system's high school graduates enrolled in a college or university by October 15 of the year after the following year, as NDE publishes it from National Student Clearinghouse records. NDE files it under the school year it reports, two years after the class graduated. In small systems a single graduate moves the rate several points.

question: Results
label: English learners scoring proficient on the ELPA
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: English Language Proficiency Assessment, all forms: the share of English learners tested who scored proficient, the level at which a student can exit English learner services. A system that exits students quickly keeps fewer advanced English learners, which lowers this rate, so read it beside the English learner gap. NDE withholds systems with few English learners.

question: Results
label: AQuESTT: share of school ratings that are Great or Excellent
unit: percent of the system's school ratings
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile; NDE has not yet released 2025-26 ratings)
note: AQuESTT, Nebraska's accountability system, classifies schools, not districts, as 1 Needs Support to Improve, 2 Good, 3 Great or 4 Excellent. A school serving more than one level (elementary, middle, high) is rated once for each. This is the share of the system's ratings that are Great or Excellent. A system with one or two schools can only be 0, 50 or 100 percent; the profile lists the ratings.

question: Results
label: Four-year graduation rate
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: class of 2026, four-year cohort (Nebraska Education Profile)
note: The share of students who entered ninth grade four years earlier (adjusted for transfers in and out) who graduated, as NDE publishes it. In small systems one student moves the rate several points, and NDE withholds the smallest cohorts.

question: Results
label: NSCAS average scale score against the state, adjusted for grade mix
unit: scale points, ELA and math averaged
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: The system's average NSCAS scale score less the score the state's students post in the same grades, ELA and mathematics averaged: for grades 3 to 8, the system's grade average less the state's, weighted by the system's tested counts. A scale score moves when students improve within a performance level, which a proficiency rate misses, and the NSCAS scale rises with grade, so grades are never mixed raw. Blank if NDE withholds any tested grade's count or score.

question: Results
label: NSCAS matched-cohort growth against the state
unit: scale points per grade, ELA and math averaged
legend: Below −6|−6 to −3|−3 to −1|−1 to +1|+1 to +3|+3 to +6|+6 or more
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: How much a grade's average scale score rose from one year to the next grade the following year, less the same rise statewide: grade 3 in 2023-24 to grade 4 in 2024-25, and so on through grade 8, over the three latest year pairs, weighted by students tested, ELA and mathematics averaged. Positive means students gained more than the state's students did. It follows grades, not the same students (families move), and counts only grade results NDE publishes. It is shown only for systems of 1,000 or more formula students: below that, a system's growth in one pair of years barely predicts the next (rank correlation 0.09 at 500 or more students, 0.24 at 1,000 or more, 0.46 at 3,000 or more), so it is mostly noise. Even at 1,000 or more, read one system's figure as a rough signal. Read it beside the level: a system can score low and grow fast.

question: Results
label: Gap between students not eligible and eligible for free or reduced-price lunch
unit: percentage points, on track or advanced, ELA and math averaged
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Percent on track or advanced for students not eligible for free or reduced-price lunch less the percent for eligible students, from NDE's own all-grades counts, ELA and mathematics averaged, for the same year as NSCAS proficiency. Larger is a wider gap. NDE withholds the result when either group is small, so it is blank in most small systems. The statewide gap is wider than most systems' gaps because it also compares students across systems.

question: Results
label: Gap between students not in special education and students in special education
unit: percentage points, on track or advanced, ELA and math averaged
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Percent on track or advanced for students not in special education less the percent for students in special education, from NDE's own all-grades counts, ELA and mathematics averaged, for the same year as NSCAS proficiency. Larger is a wider gap. NDE withholds the result when either group is small, so only the larger systems show a value. The statewide gap compares students across systems too.

question: Results
label: Gap between all other students and English learners
unit: percentage points, on track or advanced, ELA and math averaged
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: 2024-25 school year (Nebraska Education Profile, NDE all-grades totals)
note: Percent on track or advanced for students who are not English learners less the percent for English learners, from NDE's own all-grades counts, ELA and mathematics averaged, for the same year as NSCAS proficiency. NDE publishes English learners but no row for other students, so the other students are all students less English learners, by count: (all on track and advanced less English learners on track and advanced) divided by (all tested less English learners tested). Students who have left English learner services count as other students, which widens the gap. Shown only where NDE reports the English learner counts.

question: Results
label: Five-year graduation rate
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
period: class of 2025, five-year cohort (Nebraska Education Profile)
note: The share of students who entered ninth grade five years earlier (adjusted for transfers) who graduated within five years, as NDE publishes it. It is for the class a year before the four-year rate, because the fifth year has to pass first. The gap to the four-year rate for the same class is students who needed the extra year, often students in special education and English learners.

question: Results
label: Grade 11 ACT, students meeting the benchmark
unit: percent of students tested, ELA and math averaged
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Nebraska gives every eleventh grader the ACT. This is the share on track or advanced, which NDE ties to the ACT college readiness benchmarks, for English language arts and mathematics, averaged. NDE withholds the result for small grade 11 classes, so most small systems are blank; the average composite score covers more of them.

question: Results
label: Grade 11 ACT, average composite score

question: Results
label: Chronic absenteeism
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Students who missed 10% or more of the school days they were enrolled, for any reason, as a percent of students, as NDE publishes it. It is the most widely used outcome outside test scores and Nebraska's ESSA measure of school quality.

question: Teachers

source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Average teacher salary as NDE publishes it from the staff reporting each system files. Current dollars. Salaries rise with experience and degrees under most salary schedules, so read them beside those two measures.

question: Teachers

question: Teachers
label: Inexperienced teachers
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Teachers in their first three years, as a percent of all teacher FTE, from NDE's teacher quality file (the federal ESSA measure). NDE lists only the categories a system has, so a system with a published total and no inexperienced teachers shows 0%.

question: Teachers
label: Teachers on provisional credentials
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Teachers working on a provisional or emergency credential rather than a full teaching certificate, as a percent of all teacher FTE, from NDE's teacher quality file. A system with a published total and none listed shows 0%.

question: Teachers
label: Teachers teaching out of field
source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile data downloads
note: Teacher FTE assigned to a subject or grade the teacher is not endorsed for, as a percent of all teacher FTE, from NDE's teacher quality file. A system with a published total and none listed shows 0%.
